prompt: On the Cisco IOS CDP implementation documented in this chapter, the timers have not been changed. What are the default advertisement interval and advertised holdtime?
options: 60 seconds and 180 seconds
30 seconds and 120 seconds
60 seconds and 120 seconds
180 seconds and 60 seconds
explanation: The referenced IOS guide specifies an advertisement every 60 seconds and an advertised holdtime of 180 seconds. A receiver ages its entry when advertisements stop; these values can be configured.

whyWrong.1: These are the LLDP interval and holdtime documented for the chapter’s Catalyst platform.
whyWrong.2: The first number is the CDP default interval, but the default CDP holdtime is 180 seconds.
whyWrong.3: This reverses the interval and holdtime. A timer value is not a count of neighbors.

exhibit.title: Representative SW1# show lldp neighbors
exhibit.text:
Capability codes: (R) Router, (B) Bridge, (T) Telephone, (S) Station
Device ID   Local Intf  Hold-time  Capability  Port ID
DIST1       Gi0/24     120        B           Te1/0/1

prompt: Which interpretation is supported by this LLDP output?
options: DIST1 is advertising the LLDP station capability.
DIST1 advertises bridge capability and remote port Te1/0/1.
B means the receiving local port is blocked by STP.
The B code proves that DIST1 cannot also support routing.
explanation: Read the legend belonging to this protocol. LLDP B means bridge, which includes Ethernet switching. The row maps the local Gi0/24 to the advertised remote Te1/0/1; it does not establish all configured features on DIST1.

whyWrong.0: The legend uses S for station, not B.
whyWrong.2: The capability field describes the neighbor’s advertised capability, not the local STP state.
whyWrong.3: A bridge capability does not rule out other capabilities or prove how every feature is configured.

prompt: You must disable CDP only on SW1 Gi0/2 while retaining it on other intended ports. Which command belongs under interface Gi0/2?
options: no cdp run
no lldp transmit
no cdp enable
cdp timer 0
explanation: no cdp enable disables CDP on the selected interface. Keep the global cdp run setting if CDP is still needed elsewhere.

whyWrong.0: no cdp run is a global command and disables CDP device-wide.
whyWrong.1: This affects LLDP transmission, a different discovery protocol.
whyWrong.3: A timer adjustment is not the per-interface enable/disable control.

prompt: Which two privileged EXEC commands help inspect CDP advertisement/holdtime settings on the local IOS device? Choose two.
options: show cdp neighbors detail
show cdp
show cdp interface
show ip route
explanation: show cdp reports local global settings; show cdp interface reports CDP status and timing for participating local interfaces. Neighbor detail is a record about received neighbors, not a substitute for inspecting the local sender settings.

whyWrong.0: Neighbor detail can include the remaining lifetime of a received entry, but the task asks for local CDP timer settings.
whyWrong.3: The IP routing table does not report CDP timer configuration.

prompt: A supported IP phone uses LLDP-MED network-policy information from its switch. What can that information help the phone learn?
options: The phone's complete IPv4 address, subnet mask and default gateway.
The voice call server's successful registration response.
The switch's complete table of reachable IP subnets.
The intended voice VLAN and associated traffic-priority policy.
explanation: LLDP-MED extends discovery for media endpoints, including network-policy information such as voice VLAN and priority. Advertisement does not replace configuring the required VLAN, power, and data path.

whyWrong.0: Network-policy information does not replace IP address configuration or DHCP.
whyWrong.1: Advertising policy is not proof of successful call-server registration.
whyWrong.2: LLDP-MED network policy is not an IP routing-table exchange.

exhibit.title: Supplied endpoint evidence
exhibit.text:
PC-A has no CDP or LLDP agent
Its access link is up in the intended VLAN
PC-A and a same-subnet peer exchange repeated successful pings
Switch CDP/LLDP uplink neighbors refresh normally

prompt: PC-A exchanges traffic successfully but never appears in either discovery table. Which conclusion follows?
options: The user-traffic test is invalid because every host must advertise LLDP.
The access VLAN is inactive despite the successful local exchange.
The switch has proved PC-A's software is trustworthy.
Absence is expected for the stated host and does not contradict its traffic test.
explanation: A host needs a discovery speaker to advertise its identity. IP traffic can work without CDP or LLDP, and a table's absence or presence is not device authentication.

whyWrong.0: Ordinary endpoint traffic does not require a discovery agent.
whyWrong.1: The successful tested path does not support that diagnosis.
whyWrong.2: Discovery state does not authenticate software.

exhibit.title: Representative SW1# show cdp neighbors
exhibit.text:
Device ID  Local Intrfce  Holdtme  Capability  Platform    Port ID
SW2        Gig 0/1       172      S I         WS-C2960-   Gig 0/2
R1         Gig 0/2       156      R S I       CISCO2911   Gig 0/0

prompt: Which link record correctly interprets both rows?
options: SW1 Gi0/2 → SW2 Gi0/1; SW1 Gi0/0 → R1 Gi0/2
SW1 Gi0/1 → SW2 Gi0/1; SW1 Gi0/2 → R1 Gi0/2
SW1 Gi0/1 → SW2 Gi0/2; SW1 Gi0/2 → R1 Gi0/0
SW2 Gi0/1 → R1 Gi0/0; SW1 Gi0/2 has no neighbor
explanation: The command ran on SW1. Local Intrfce belongs to SW1; Port ID is the interface advertised by the neighbor in that row. Record both device names and both ports.

whyWrong.0: This reverses local and remote port ownership and invents an SW1 Gi0/0 observation.
whyWrong.1: The remote ports are Gi0/2 on SW2 and Gi0/0 on R1, not copies of the local port numbers.
whyWrong.3: The table reports two SW1 adjacencies; it does not report a link between SW2 and R1.

exhibit.title: Recorded interface state on the connected ports
exhibit.text:
SW1 Gi0/1: LLDP Tx enabled; Rx enabled
SW2 Gi0/2: LLDP Tx disabled; Rx enabled

prompt: LLDP runs globally on both switches, the cable is correct, and old entries have expired. What is the expected neighbor-table result?
options: Neither switch learns the other because LLDP requires bidirectional transmission.
Both switches learn each other because global enablement overrides interface settings.
SW1 learns SW2, but SW2 cannot learn SW1.
SW2 learns SW1, but SW1 cannot learn SW2.
explanation: SW1 transmits, so SW2 can receive and learn SW1. SW2 does not transmit, so SW1 receives no new SW2 advertisement. Receive and transmit controls are independent.

whyWrong.0: One-way LLDP learning is possible when the corresponding sender and receiver are enabled.
whyWrong.1: Global enablement does not override a disabled per-interface transmit direction.
whyWrong.2: This reverses the direction: SW2 is the device with transmission disabled.

prompt: A fresh CDP detail entry advertises SW2 management address 192.168.12.12, but SW1 cannot ping it. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Discovery works; IP reachability requires separate checks.
The management path is working because discovery crossed the link.
The management address must be on the port facing SW1.
CDP authenticated SW2 and verified its SSH service.
explanation: CDP operates at Layer 2 and can advertise an address that is not on the facing interface. The entry is discovery evidence, not proof of IP reachability, identity authentication, or a working SSH service.

whyWrong.1: A received Layer 2 advertisement does not test the separate IP management path.
whyWrong.2: A device can advertise a management address from another interface.
whyWrong.3: Ordinary CDP advertisements do not authenticate the neighbor or test a management service.

prompt: A policy prohibits discovery on an untrusted provider-facing Ethernet port. Internal switch and phone links still require their approved discovery features. Which change best matches the policy?
options: Disable both discovery protocols globally on the switch.
Disable CDP on the port while leaving LLDP participation enabled.
Disable both discovery protocols on the port and preserve approved internal use.
Disable only LLDP transmission on the port and leave other discovery enabled.
explanation: Apply the boundary policy to the selected interface. Review both discovery protocols, because disabling one does not disable the other. Preserve approved dependencies on other ports and verify their behavior.

whyWrong.0: The requirement is port-specific; a global change removes approved internal discovery.
whyWrong.1: That leaves LLDP participating where all discovery is prohibited.
whyWrong.3: That leaves reception and CDP participation outside the stated policy.

prompt: An IOS switch supports LLDP but show lldp reports that it is not enabled. You want discovery only on the approved Gi0/1 uplink. What is the appropriate next configuration?
options: Enter cdp run; LLDP automatically shares CDP’s state.
Enable lldp run, Gi0/1 transmit/receive, and verify port policy.
Add a default route; the LLDP process starts when a gateway is reachable.
Only enter lldp receive on Gi0/1; the global process can remain disabled.
explanation: Enable the LLDP process and the intended interface directions. Inspect other interface states rather than assuming a universal default across models or releases.

whyWrong.0: CDP and LLDP have independent configuration.
whyWrong.2: LLDP is Layer 2 and does not need a default route.
whyWrong.3: An interface direction setting cannot make a globally disabled LLDP process operate.

prompt: The sender advertises a 180-second CDP holdtime. A receiver’s countdown is now approximately 174 seconds. What does that indicate?
options: The link has been down for exactly 174 seconds.
The sender will transmit its next advertisement in 174 seconds.
The neighbor was discovered for the first time 174 seconds ago.
About 6 seconds have elapsed since the advertisement that last refreshed this entry.
explanation: 180 − 174 = 6 seconds. The countdown describes the entry’s remaining lifetime after its last refresh; rounding and display timing make this an approximate observation. It does not establish physical link uptime.

whyWrong.0: The countdown is time remaining, not downtime.
whyWrong.1: The receiver’s cache countdown is separate from the sender’s advertisement schedule.
whyWrong.2: A refresh restarts the lifetime of an existing entry, so this is not an age-since-first-discovery value.

prompt: Global configuration explicitly contains `no cdp run`, but Gi0/1 contains `cdp enable`. What should you conclude?
options: CDP remains disabled globally; the interface command does not override that.
Gi0/1 operates CDP while every other interface stays disabled.
Only CDP reception works on Gi0/1.
The device automatically changes to LLDP on Gi0/1.
explanation: CDP needs the global process and the interface enabled. Global disablement prevents CDP operation even where the interface has cdp enable.

whyWrong.1: Per-interface enablement does not override the global state.
whyWrong.2: CDP does not use LLDP-style independent transmit and receive controls here.
whyWrong.3: One discovery protocol does not automatically substitute for the other.

prompt: Two devices appear as CDP neighbors, but inspection finds an Ethernet hub between them. What is the correct documentation conclusion?
options: The hub must have an IP address in the CDP table before the observation can be valid.
Document the speakers and hub; discovery does not prove a single cable.
The hub is necessarily the Device ID shown in each CDP row.
Every unmanaged switch must forward LLDP in exactly the same way.
explanation: A hub repeats the received signal and does not identify itself through CDP. Neighbor discovery can therefore omit an intermediate nonparticipating component. Record observed speakers separately from verified physical infrastructure.

whyWrong.0: A hub does not need an IP address or CDP identity to repeat signals.
whyWrong.2: The Device ID belongs to the advertising speaker, not automatically to an intermediate device.
whyWrong.3: Do not generalize this CDP/hub case to all bridges or to LLDP forwarding behavior.

exhibit.title: Supplied protocol checks
exhibit.text:
Physical connection up; intended interfaces verified
SW1: CDP enabled; LLDP globally disabled
SW2: LLDP globally enabled, Tx/Rx enabled; CDP disabled
Policy: use LLDP on this link

prompt: Both images support both protocols, but their empty discovery tables persist after sufficient advertisement time. Which change establishes the approved LLDP discovery on this link?
options: Change both management gateways to the same router address.
Enable CDP on SW2 while leaving SW1's LLDP disabled.
Enable LLDP globally and in both directions on SW1's connected port.
Clear both tables repeatedly while keeping their protocol settings.
explanation: The devices currently use different discovery protocols. Enable the approved common protocol, LLDP, at SW1 and verify both directions; IP addressing and table clears do not translate CDP into LLDP.

whyWrong.0: The Layer 2 protocol mismatch is independent of the management gateway.
whyWrong.1: That could provide CDP discovery, but the approved outcome requires LLDP and SW1's LLDP process remains disabled.
whyWrong.3: Clearing tables does not create compatible advertisements.

exhibit.title: Supplied complete relevant direction state
exhibit.text:
LLDP globally enabled on both devices; link up
SW1: transmit enabled, receive disabled
SW2: transmit disabled, receive enabled
Old entries have expired

prompt: The required outcome is that SW1 receives fresh SW2 information. Which two interface changes are necessary under the stated configuration? Choose two.
options: Enable LLDP transmit on SW1.
Enable LLDP receive on SW1.
Enable LLDP receive on SW2.
Enable LLDP transmit on SW2.
Disable CDP on both switches.
explanation: SW2 is the sender for this observation and SW1 is the receiver. Restore those two disabled directions; the reverse-direction controls already work and CDP is independent.

whyWrong.0: SW1 transmission is already enabled and sends information in the opposite direction.
whyWrong.2: SW2 reception is already enabled and concerns learning SW1.
whyWrong.4: CDP need not be disabled for LLDP to operate.

exhibit.title: Supplied maintenance records
exhibit.text:
09:00 drawing: SW1 Gi0/1 to SW2 Gi0/2
09:02 saved CDP record: same endpoints
09:10 cable move recorded, destination port not recorded
09:11 new SW1 LLDP record: neighbor name SW2, remote Gi0/1
No post-move SW2 observation or physical-port inspection has yet been recorded

prompt: Which documentation action is justified now?
options: Replace the approved drawing with the oldest cached observation.
Record the disagreement and confirm current identities and both port ends before updating the drawing.
Declare Gi0/1 physically faulty because two records disagree.
Publish the new one-sided record immediately because it has the latest timestamp.
explanation: The observations were taken at different times and the new local record lacks corroboration. Preserve the evidence and establish the current physical endpoints and peer identity before publishing a correction.

whyWrong.0: The old record predates the move and may no longer describe the current connection.
whyWrong.2: An identity or port-record conflict alone does not establish a physical-layer fault.
whyWrong.3: The newer record is useful evidence, but its identity and physical endpoint still need corroboration.
